q: Which of the following banking concepts emphasises the delivery of banking services at an affordable cost to the disadvantaged and low-income sections?
explain: Financial inclusion is defined as delivery of banking services at affordable cost, using ‘no-frills’ accounts, to disadvantaged and low-income groups.

q: Which of the following is NOT an aim behind pushing financial inclusion in rural and semi-urban India?
options: Plugging leaks in subsidies through direct transfers
explain: Inclusion seeks to reduce, not raise, dependence on informal credit such as moneylenders. Savings, formal credit and plugging subsidy leaks are its three main goals.

q: As financial inclusion spreads, capital formation is expected to rise because people move their savings away from
options: Land, buildings and bullion towards bank products
Bank deposits towards cash at home
Government schemes towards informal chit funds
explain: Traditional parking of savings in land, buildings and bullion is unproductive; bank deposits channel savings into capital formation.

q: The unbanked population has traditionally depended mainly on which source of credit?
explain: Without access to banks, the unbanked rely on informal channels such as family, friends and moneylenders; formal credit is meant to replace this.

q: Why does the government push for direct cash transfers into bank accounts?
options: To increase taxes collected from the poor
To close all rural bank branches
To reduce leakage of subsidies and welfare money meant for the poor
To replace the RBI’s role in credit
explain: Much of the money meant for the poorest never reaches them. Direct transfers into accounts plug these gaps and leaks.

q: Banks use the business correspondent (BC) model mainly in areas where
options: Customers do not need banking services
Interest rates are fixed by the government
Opening a brick-and-mortar branch is too costly
explain: BCs take banking to the doorstep in areas where banks cannot justify the cost of a physical branch, giving affordable access to the unbanked.

q: Which statement about the business correspondent scheme is correct?
options: BCs handle cash deposits, small credit and recovery of loans on behalf of the bank
BCs can only be used in metropolitan cities
BCs are regulated as separate banks
explain: The BC model covers several services including cash deposit, small credit and recovery. Saying BCs only disburse credit is incomplete and therefore wrong.

q: Which of the following types of bank accounts offers low-cost access to banking for lower-income customers?
options: Regular savings account with minimum balance
explain: A no-frills account cuts out unneeded extras and keeps basic deposit and withdrawal, making it a low-cost route into banking.

q: Under the Swabhiman campaign, habitations are covered if the population is more than
options: 2,000 in plain areas and 1,000 in north-eastern and hilly states
explain: Swabhiman covers habitations above 2,000 in plains and above 1,000 in north-eastern and hilly states (2011 Census), using the BC model.

q: Which of the following was introduced by NABARD from 1998-99 to give farmers timely, hassle-free short-term credit for crop production?
explain: The Kisan Credit Card meets production credit and short-term needs of farmers. The Lead Bank Scheme is a district-level coordination arrangement from 1969.

q: In which year was the Lead Bank Scheme introduced?
explain: The Lead Bank Scheme dates from 1969. 1979 is when the Lead Bank Officer was appointed, and 1996 saw Local Area Banks.

q: Which of the following metropolitan cities was exempted from the Lead Bank Scheme?
explain: All districts except the metropolitan cities of Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and some Union Territories were allotted to lead banks.

q: The Lead Bank Officer (LBO), who prepares District Credit Plans and monitors them, is now designated as the
explain: The LBO, appointed in 1979, is now called the Lead District Manager.

q: Local Area Banks were introduced in which year?
explain: Local Area Banks were set up in 1996 to bridge the credit gap in rural and semi-urban areas.

q: Which statement about Local Area Banks is correct?
options: They operate across the whole country
They may perform all functions of a scheduled commercial bank within a limited area
explain: Local Area Banks have a limited geographical area but can do all functions of a scheduled commercial bank, and may need a higher CAR (above 15 %) for the risk.

q: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK) was set up mainly to
options: Facilitate credit support to poor women for their socio-economic upliftment
explain: RMK provides credit support to poor women. It is a credit-support body, not a regulator or insurer.

q: Which of the following programmes aims at promoting savings among rural women?
explain: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was meant to promote thrift among rural women; Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is about credit support.

q: A textile company borrows at 10 % and the government gives a 2 % interest subvention. What interest does the textile company effectively pay?
explain: Subvention reduces the cost: 10 % minus 2 % equals 8 %, while sectors without subvention pay the full 10 %.

q: A farmer borrows from a bank at 10 % and receives a 4 % interest subvention from the government. The effective rate is
explain: 10 % less the 4 % government subvention gives 6 %.

q: In the Differential Rate of Interest (DRI) system, certain sectors get loans at
options: A rate lower than the base rate
A rate higher than the base rate
The same rate as the repo rate
A floating rate fixed by the borrower
explain: DRI loans (for example education, export credit, agriculture and weaker sections) are priced below the base rate.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the broad categories of priority sector lending listed for scheduled commercial banks?
explain: Priority sectors include agriculture, small-scale industries, small business or service enterprises, micro credit, education and housing. Speculation is not one of them.

q: Priority sector lending aims at
options: All-round development of the economy by directing credit to specified sectors
Reducing the number of bank accounts
explain: PSL makes banks lend a set portion to important sectors, aiming for broad-based development rather than just the financial sector.

q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is run by which department?
options: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
explain: PMJDY, India’s National Mission for Financial Inclusion, is run by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

q: According to the book, what accidental insurance cover comes with a PMJDY account?
explain: The book gives ₹1 lakh as the accidental insurance cover under PMJDY. ₹3 lakh is not a feature of the scheme as described.

q: After how many months of opening a PMJDY account does the holder become eligible for an overdraft of ₹5,000?
explain: PMJDY account holders become eligible for a ₹5,000 overdraft after six months of opening the account.

q: What is the full form of NUUP, through which mobile banking for the poor is made available?
explain: NUUP stands for National Unified USSD Platform; it lets people use basic phones for banking, not only smartphones.

q: Which of the following is promoted through the National Unified USSD Platform?
explain: NUUP enables mobile banking on ordinary phones, a facility earlier limited to smartphones.

q: Which of the following is a feature of a PMJDY account?
explain: PMJDY accounts carry no minimum balance requirement and come with a RuPay debit card.

q: Which statement is correct about the Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA)?
options: It requires a minimum balance of ₹500
All existing no-frills accounts were converted into BSBDA under RBI’s 2012 guidelines
The holder can open another savings account in the same bank freely
It allows unlimited withdrawals every month
explain: BSBDA has a zero minimum balance, limits withdrawals to four a month, and replaced all existing no-frills accounts under the 2012 RBI guidelines.

q: What is the maximum number of withdrawals (including ATM withdrawals) allowed in a month in a BSBDA?
explain: BSBDA holders are allowed a maximum of four withdrawals a month; deposits have no limit.

q: In a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account, the number of deposits that can be made in a month is
explain: There is no limit on the number of deposits, but withdrawals are restricted to four a month.

q: If a customer already has a savings account in a bank and opens a BSBDA there, within how many days must the old savings account be closed?
explain: A BSBDA holder cannot hold another savings account in that bank; an existing one must be closed within 30 days.

q: How many Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts can an individual hold?
explain: A person can hold only one BSBDA (and no other savings account in that bank), though term and recurring deposits are allowed.

q: Which of the following BSBDA holders’ facilities is allowed in the same bank?
options: A fixed deposit or recurring deposit
explain: A BSBDA holder may still keep term (fixed) deposits and recurring deposits in the same bank, but not another savings account.

q: Which statement about payments banks is correct?
options: They can give large corporate loans
They accept deposits from the public but do not lend
They are meant only for large businesses
explain: Payments banks offer payment services and deposit products to small businesses and low-income households but do not lend.

q: Which of the following was among the four functional payments banks mentioned in the book?
explain: The book names Paytm, Airtel, India Post Payments Bank and Fino as functional payments banks; the others are not payments banks. Counts like this change over time.

q: Which statement about small finance banks is correct?
options: They can accept deposits and also lend
They are not allowed to deal with the public
They do not exist in India
explain: Small finance banks are niche banks that provide basic banking, which includes both accepting deposits and lending.

q: RBI’s policy on financial literacy is that financial inclusion should
options: Go hand in hand with financial literacy
explain: RBI wants inclusion and literacy to progress together, supporting Financial Literacy and Credit Counselling Centres (FLCCs).

q: The Khan Commission was set up in 2004 to
options: Prepare a report on financial inclusion
Review the financial status of public sector banks
explain: RBI set up the Khan Commission in 2004 to look into financial inclusion; its ideas fed the 2005-06 mid-term review and the no-frills account push.

q: The Committee on Financial Inclusion headed by Dr C. Rangarajan was set up in
explain: The Government of India constituted the Rangarajan Committee in 2006; the Khan Commission came earlier, in 2004.

q: Dr C. Rangarajan, who headed the 2006 Committee on Financial Inclusion, was at that time the
options: Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister
explain: Dr Rangarajan was then Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

q: NaMFI, proposed by the Rangarajan Committee, stands for
explain: NaMFI is the National Mission on Financial Inclusion, to pursue universal inclusion in a specific time frame with all stakeholders.

q: The National Rural Financial Inclusion Plan (NRFIP) targeted access to comprehensive financial services for at least what share of financially excluded households by 2012?
explain: NRFIP aimed at 50 % of excluded households (about 55.77 million) by 2012, with the rest to be covered by 2015.

q: Under the NRFIP, semi-urban and rural branches of banks were advised to cover at least how many new households per branch per year?
explain: A minimum target of 250 new cultivator and non-cultivator households per branch per annum was suggested.

q: Which of the following is NOT a main reason for lack of financial inclusion?
options: Too many bank branches in villages
explain: The four reasons are collateral, poor credit absorption, inadequate reach of institutions and a weak community network. Excess branches is not one of them.

q: The Rangarajan Committee suggested organising the urban and peri-urban poor into
explain: Like the rural poor, urban and peri-urban poor should be organised into Neighbourhood Groups, which would need NABARD’s mandate to extend beyond rural areas.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low Income Households was set up by the RBI in
explain: RBI set up the Mor Committee in September 2013. July 2015 is the Mohanty Committee and 1 January 2016 was Mor’s target date for universal accounts.

q: According to the Nachiket Mor Committee, every adult should have a bank account by
explain: The committee recommended a universal bank account for all Indians above 18 years by 1 January 2016.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee recommended wholesale banks for credit outreach, requiring capital of
explain: Wholesale banks were to have ₹50 crore of capital, a tenth of what applied to new full banks.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee recommended raising the priority sector lending mandate from 40 per cent to
explain: The committee proposed a 50 % priority sector target, adjusted for sectors and regions by difficulty of lending.

q: Which pair of district-level ratios did the Nachiket Mor Committee propose to monitor meaningful financial inclusion?
explain: Mor suggested credit-to-GDP and life cover-to-GDP ratios, moving beyond merely counting accounts.

q: Which committee suggested initiatives on the medium-term path for financial inclusion?
explain: The Deepak Mohanty Committee was asked to draw a five-year (medium-term) action plan for financial inclusion.

q: On what date did the RBI constitute the 14-member Deepak Mohanty Committee on financial inclusion?
explain: The committee was constituted on 15 July 2015 under RBI Executive Director Deepak Mohanty.

q: Which of the following was recommended by the Deepak Mohanty Committee?
options: Link Aadhaar to every individual account as a unique biometric identifier
Stop account opening drives for women
explain: The committee wanted Aadhaar linked to each account, more mobile technology, and special efforts for women’s accounts; it wanted agri interest subvention phased out.

q: Which of these committees on financial inclusion was constituted by the Government of India rather than the RBI?
explain: The Rangarajan Committee (2006) was constituted by the Government of India. The other three were set up by the RBI.

q: What is the loan limit of the MUDRA scheme category Tarun?
explain: Tarun covers loans from ₹5 lakh up to ₹10 lakh, the maximum under MUDRA. Shishu is up to ₹50,000 and Kishore up to ₹5 lakh.

q: What is the Jan Samarth Portal?
options: A digital platform linking government-sponsored credit schemes to lenders
An online database of health-care data
explain: Jan Samarth, an initiative of the Ministry of Finance, connects beneficiaries directly to lenders under over a dozen government credit schemes.

q: Which of the following is NOT a basic principle of microfinance loans?
explain: Microfinance rests on small loans, lack of physical collateral, peer monitoring and a focus on women. Large loans go against the idea.

q: Which board established by the RBI encourages transparency in lending and fair pricing by banks?
options: Banking Codes and Standards Board of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
explain: The BCSBI promotes fair practice codes for transparency in lending and pricing. The Banks Board Bureau deals with appointments of top bank personnel.

q: Which focus area is monitored by the Banks Board Bureau?
options: Framing strict norms to stop NPAs
explain: The Banks Board Bureau focuses on selecting and appointing top bank personnel. It does not set rates or write Basel norms.

q: Loans of very small amounts given to low-income groups are called
explain: Micro credit refers to very small loans to low-income groups; cash credit and overdraft are working-capital facilities.

q: Which bodies made the initial contribution for setting up the Financial Inclusion Fund?
options: Government of India, RBI and NABARD
SIDBI, Government of India and IDBI Bank
explain: The Financial Inclusion Fund was set up with initial contributions from the Government of India, RBI and NABARD.

q: Under MUDRA, which category covers loans above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh?
explain: Kishore covers ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh. Shishu goes up to ₹50,000 and Tarun from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
